name: T3 Planner
one_liner: An LLM proposes robot waypoints and controller code, a temporal-logic checker scores them, and failures go back until a plan passes.

loop.proposes: Subgoal waypoints, timed waypoints and a Python controller script, written by an LLM in three stages
loop.judged_by: Signal Temporal Logic robustness checks, a Python syntax check, and simulation of the controller on annotated cases
loop.steers: A failed output goes back to the LLM as the previous failed result, until all checks pass

headline_result: In simulated household, chip-design and navigation scenarios, success rates with GPT-4o were 91.65%, 91.60% and 83.69%, against 56.67%, 61.29% and 50.00% for AutoTAMP with GPT-4o. The authors claim a 30 to 40% improvement.
caveat: All scenarios are in a simulated 2D environment with no real-robot tests, and the paper gives no retry limit. The checker is a temporal-logic verifier, not model predictive control, and this is a single preprint with no venue listed.
beyond_harness_note: A formal temporal-logic verifier, not an LLM judge, decides whether each proposed plan is valid.
generative_model: Pretrained LLMs (GPT-4o, DeepSeek-reasoner, Gemini-2.5-Pro), plus a distilled Qwen3-4B
algorithmic_authority: Signal Temporal Logic robustness computation and simulation of the generated controller

sources.title: T3 Planner: A Self-Correcting LLM Framework for Robotic Motion Planning with Temporal Logic (arXiv:2510.16767)

verification.notes: Found by searching for LLM trajectory generators with a checker that feeds back. Read the arXiv abstract page and HTML full text. The checker is an STL verifier, so this does not satisfy the draft's MPC/safety-filter wording; I found no primary source with an MPC checker feeding back into the next proposal. Evidence is thin (v1 only, authors unaffiliated on the page, simulation only). Table II numbers used; an ablation elsewhere quotes 96% for chip, which the paper does not reconcile. Include only if the site accepts a preprint-level robotics example. 'validity_scope: formal' applies to the STL checks, while controllers are validated by simulation. Org not printed in arXiv HTML or abstract; set to first author per rule, never guessed (review 2026-11-03).
